column1: # Accepted findings of noreturn_audit.py (decision 0204). One row per finding: kind<TAB>name<TAB>file<TAB>reason. `reason` starts with a tag that the tool checks:
#   not-gen-visible: the declaring header must stay outside the include closure of the generated units (otherwise the row no longer matches and the test fails)
#   opt-in-macro:    the declaration must stay conditional on an opt-in macro (FLE_GMHEX_RETURNS)
# A row that matches nothing any more is itself a failure (remove it). A finding without a row is a failure (fix the declaration or the wrapper, or add a row with its reason).
# kind=returns: a `__wrap_<name>` (or a strong definition of <name>) in `file` has a path that returns although <name> is declared noreturn in a runtime header.

column4: not-gen-visible: fle_imp_RtlPcToFileHeader is declared noreturn in fle_proc.h, which no generated unit includes (the generator writes fle_runtime.h fle_sse.h fle_dispatch.h and fle_modules.h/fle_seh.h/fle_flags_nf.h/fle_prune.h/fle_vmap.h only), and the generated C declares the import as a plain `void fle_imp_RtlPcToFileHeader(void);`. So no caller compiled from generated C assumes it stops; no C file of runtime/ or harness/ calls it directly. The wrapper answers the API, as intended (S-vst-*). If a header of the closure ever includes fle_proc.h this row stops matching and the test fails.
